title: Enzo Fernandez ‘very happy’ at Chelsea, Trevoh Chalobah out for six weeks – Rosenior
content:
Liam Rosenior has said Enzo Fernandez is “very happy” at Chelsea despite the midfielder casting doubt on his future after their Champions League loss to Paris Saint-Germain.

Fernandez’s contract runs until 2032 but he said on Tuesday “we’ll see” and remained non-committal when asked if he could guarantee staying at Stamford Bridge past the summer.

The head coach, speaking at his news conference on Tuesday, said he had spoken to the Argentina international.

“(Fernandez) made it really, really clear to me how happy he is here at this club, how much he wants to win, how passionate he is for us to be successful,” Rosenior said. “So for me, he’s fully committed to this group, he’s fully committed to winning here at this football club.”

Rosenior also said that Chalobah will be out for a period of “maybe six weeks” with a “serious injury” to his right ankle. The issue means the England international will be ruled out of Thomas Tuchel’s squad for the March games, the last before the provisional World Cup squad is named.

The centre-back suffered the injury in a tackle from PSG’s Achraf Hakimi in the final ten minutes of their 3-0 second leg defeat. Chalobah was taken off on a stretcher and later posted a photo to his social media of his foot pointing behind him saying his ankle “should be broken”.

Rosenior said after the match that the 26-year-old was “really worried” but said on Thursday that “it’s nowhere near as serious as we first feared”.

Chalobah has been a regular in Chelsea’s starting line-up, only coming on as a substitute in three of his 44 appearances this term.

His injury is the second significant blow to Rosenior’s back line after The Athletic reported that Reece James has sustained another hamstring injury on Monday and will be out for several weeks.

Filip Jorgensen is also expected to be out for “a matter of weeks” the head coach said, after a “minor operation” on a groin injury picked up against PSG. Rosenior said “the hope” is for Levi Colwill to return this season from his anterior cruciate ligament injury following his return to the training pitch, but that “he’s still looking at a good while yet”.
